result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B keeps all three previously studied units in daily closed-book recall from week 1 and uses mixed question sets every Saturday. It also leaves exam-specific details as placeholders for the learner to fill in. A is easier to read on a fridge, but it reviews old units in blocks and leaves law and ethics out of weeks 1–2. It also relies on 'read and take notes' sessions and assumes the exam is the PTCE with a 60–70 minute practice-exam length. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers stay within the time budget and teach the three untouched units in Weeks 1–3. A keeps the units already covered coming back almost every day through closed-book recall, while B mostly works in blocks and brings each old unit back only once or twice before the mixed weeks. A also puts the whole plan in one fridge-friendly table and leaves blanks for exam details instead of assuming the PTCE and its timing.
